title: GTA6 IGN Interview Details Revealed: Freedom & NPC Upgrades
description: A recent community-discussed IGN interview with Rockstar's Rob Nelson reveals exciting new details about GTA6 mission structures, dual-protagonist mechanics, and advanced NPC interactions.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## New IGN Interview Details with Rob Nelson Shed Light on GTA6 Design Philosophy

Details from a comprehensive interview between IGN and Rockstar's Rob Nelson have surfaced within the community, offering exciting new information regarding the highly anticipated *Grand Theft Auto VI*. While expanding on concepts previously hinted at, the interview provides a clearer picture of how Rockstar aims to reshape open-world design.

### Less Restrictive Missions and Blurs in Scripting

A major focus for Rockstar in GTA6 is making story missions less restrictive where possible. Certain missions will feature multiple escape routes, and police chases or robberies can seamlessly transition into the same systemic gameplay found in free roam.

Despite this push toward player freedom, Rockstar still intends to utilize tightly directed cinematic sequences when necessary, meaning missions will not devolve into completely unguided sandbox experiences. One of their primary goals is to blur the line between scripted missions and free-roam gameplay. Emergent free-roam sequences can reportedly look and feel almost like scripted missions, particularly when Jason and Lucia coordinate during heists and escapes.

### Safehouses, Daily Routines, and Hair Growth

Safehouses in GTA 6 draw heavy inspiration from the camp system in *Red Dead Redemption 2*. Jason and Lucia will maintain their own daily schedules while at home and interact realistically with one another.

Additionally, aesthetic upkeep returns: Jason can trim his hair and beard shorter while at home. However, changing styles entirely or growing hair longer will still require a visit to a professional barber, suggesting a refined version of RDR2's dynamic hair growth system.

### Dual-Protagonist Dynamics

Rockstar describes the world of GTA 6 as its largest, deepest, most densely populated, and complex environment to date. Players can freely switch between Jason and Lucia during much of free roam, and the character not currently under direct control will continue living out their routine rather than idling.

Players can text and call the other protagonist, with ignored messages having a minor negative impact on their relationship. When traveling together, Jason and Lucia actively protect each other, intervening in confrontations and assisting during escapes—such as one driving while the other shoots at pursuers.

### Advanced NPC Interaction and Combat Escalation

The NPC interaction system from RDR2 returns in a significantly more advanced form, backed by dedicated writing and directing resources to generate vast amounts of ambient dialogue. Combat encounters also feature broader levels of escalation, allowing players to threaten targets into backing down, knock them out, incapacitate them non-fatally, or eliminate them entirely.

---

### Editor's Take

These newly detailed insights indicate that Rockstar is successfully bridging the gap between the meticulous environmental storytelling of *Red Dead Redemption 2* and the frantic urban sandbox of the GTA universe. By emphasizing living in the world rather than just checking off mission objectives, GTA6 is shaping up to be an unprecedentedly dynamic living ecosystem.
